title: Dynamical Generation of Rectified Electric Current
abstract: Rectification is a fundamental nonlinear transport process that converts an alternating drive into a direct current. In this work, we propose a general theoretical framework for electric current rectification triggered by a dynamical external drive that couples to an arbitrary well-defined operator of a periodic system, and which in the static limit forbids any steady current. In the dynamical regime, the finite frequency $Ω$ of the time-varying drive breaks time-translation invariance and injects energy into the system, enabling a second-order {\it nonlinear rectified} current that has no static counterpart. This rectification process has two distinct origins: (i) an impurity-scattering-modified distribution function at finite frequency, and (ii) a time-domain anomalous velocity stemming from a dynamical mixed Berry curvature. Both contributions persist when the driving frequency lies well below the optical transition gap. Applying our general theory to a buckled magnetic system subject to an out-of-plane oscillating electric field, we characterize the generated current as a {\it nonlinear magnetoelectric gyrotropic effect} and predict that the induced rectified current is sensitive to the magnetic order, thereby offering a feasible electrical probe of Néel order in non-coplanar antiferromagnets.
summary: This paper develops a general theory for how an oscillating external field can induce a steady, rectified electric current in a periodic system, even if the static case forbids it. The resulting DC current is shown to have both extrinsic (impurity-related) and intrinsic (Berry curvature-derived) origins. By applying this framework to magnetic materials, the authors propose that this effect can act as a novel electrical probe for detecting specific types of magnetic ordering.
main_problem: The work addresses the nonlinear transport phenomenon of electric current rectification, converting an alternating external drive into a steady direct current (DC) even when static theory forbids it.
main_result: A general theoretical framework is established showing that this rectified DC current arises from two distinct contributions: impurity scattering and a dynamical mixed Berry curvature. This effect can serve as a sensitive electrical probe for magnetic order, such as Néel ordering in antiferromagnets.
method: The analysis uses a semiclassical approach, expanding the system's response to the time-varying drive ($\lambda(t)$) up to second order in the drive amplitude to isolate the DC component. The theory decomposes the current into extrinsic (scattering-dependent) and intrinsic (Berry curvature-derived) parts.
model_or_system: The general model involves Bloch electrons in a periodic system driven by an external oscillating field coupling to an arbitrary operator $\hat{O}$. A specific application is studied using a tight-binding Hamiltonian for a buckled magnetic lattice subjected to an out-of-plane oscillating electric field.
key_observables: Rectified DC current ($J_{dc}$), which is proportional to the product of two drive amplitudes ($\lambda_a\lambda_b$), and its components $\sigma_{	ext{abc}}^{	ext{ex}}$ (extrinsic) and $\sigma_{	ext{abc}}^{	ext{in}}$ (intrinsic).
important_parameters: The driving frequency ($\Omega$) relative to the optical transition gap ($\Delta_{	ext{gap}}$), and the scattering rate ($\Gamma$). The DC current persists even when $\hbar\Omega \ll \Delta_{	ext{gap}}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the semiclassical framework, utilizing the relaxation-time approximation for the distribution function. Some derivations employ a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the generation of $J_{dc}$ from an oscillating drive. Figure 2 shows the scaling behavior of different conductivity components ($\sigma_{	ext{ex,1}}$, $\sigma_{	ext{ex,2}}$, $\sigma_{	ext{in}}$) across various frequency regimes relative to the scattering rate. Figure 3 depicts the physical realization in a buckled honeycomb lattice.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general theory for rectification, derives the current components ($\sigma^{	ext{ex}}, \sigma^{	ext{in}}$), analyzes their frequency dependence and symmetry constraints (P, T, PT), and concludes with a specific application to magnetic systems to probe Néel order.
why_interesting: The concept of generating DC currents from AC drives via nonlinear coupling is central to understanding non-equilibrium quantum transport. The explicit connection between this effect and measurable magnetic orders makes it highly relevant for condensed matter theorists studying emergent phenomena in frustrated magnets.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of rectified current generation by a dynamical drive λ(t) coupled to a local operator ˆO. At times t < 0, the system is in equilibrium. The drive is adia- batically turned on during the interval −∞< t < t1, reaching a finite amplitude with zero frequency for t1 < t < 0. While a static component of the drive would merely redistribute carri- ers, leading to a modified steady-state distribution, the finite frequency Ωat t > 0 enables the generation of a rectified DC current Jdc.

FIG. 2. Schematic depiction of the extrinsic (σex,1 and σex,2) and intrinsic (σin) DC current and their symmetry properties. Γ denotes the scattering rate, making σex,1 term dominate and suppressing σex,2 in the clean limit. However, the intrinsic one is disorder free and may dominate gradually in the dirty limit.

FIG. 3. (a) Schematic illustration of the buckled honeycomb lattice with N´eel order. In the side view, the two sublattice atoms (A and B) form a vertical dipole moment that couples to an out-of-plane electric field Ez. (b) Band structure along the high-symmetry lines, featuring a band gap of ∼50 meV. (c) Momentum-space distribution of the vertical dipole moment ⟨ˆpz⟩ for the valence band. (d) and (e) Calculated σex,1 and σin as functions of Fermi energy µ. (f) Angular dependence of σex,1 at µ = 18 meV on the N´eel vector direction; the evolution of the spin texture on the A and B sublattices is also depicted. Parameters used: t = 30 meV, λR = 0.1t, Jex = 0.3t, and temperature T = 5 K.
